title: How to organise the canned and jarred goods | Pantry
description:
Holds the cans and jars that turn an empty-fridge week into dinner.

This is the Canned and Jarred Goods in the Pantry. About 30-45 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
Cans sit in rows on risers with every label facing you: tomatoes together, beans together, soup together. No dented seams, no domed lids, no jar hidden behind another jar, and the oldest date in each row standing at the front of it.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Take every can and jar out, turn each one until you find the date, and put the dented, rusted and bulging ones
Straighten: Rows by meal rather than by size.
Shine: Wipe the sticky rings where a honey jar or a sauce lid has wept, and wash the threads of the jars you open mos
Safety: Poison, choke, or strangle: a can with a domed lid, a weeping seam, or a hiss as it opens is spoiled rather th
Standardize: Label each row with its category and put the back row up on a riser so it sits above the front row.
Sustain: When you sit down to write the shopping list, walk the can rows first and read the gaps.

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
Every label faces out, every row holds one category, and the oldest date sits at the front of its row.
